**Finding: Compliant — no redline proposed.**

Section 24 already delivers our preferred ASSIGN position:

- **24.1** — We may assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor (merger, reorganization, acquisition, sale of all or substantially all assets) without Vendor consent; prompt notice plus assignee assumption only.
- **24.2** — Vendor is restricted asymmetrically: no assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without our prior written consent (reasonableness qualifier runs in our favour), and never to a direct competitor of ours.
- **24.3** — The mutual consent requirement is expressly scoped to "other assignments," so it does not claw back the 24.1 carve-out (the planner's concern checks out clean).
- **24.4** — Our change of control gives Vendor no right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service, and Vendor must cooperate with successor administrative changes.
- **13.3** — Licence rights travel with a permitted assignment, so the 13.1 non-transferability language does not strand us post-M&A.

No change-of-control trigger appears anywhere else; Section 9 termination rights are limited to breach, insolvency, security/legal failures, and our convenience right.
